plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing auctions you could have profitably won. With a value of $31, bidding exactly $31 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win whenever profitable and never overpay.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid one's true value, regardless of others' strategies. This is because bidding value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable) and lose otherwise, avoiding both overpaying and missing profitable wins. With no prior history to suggest deviation, and since this is a one-shot game, I will bid my true value of $37.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This holds true whether opponents are truthful, aggressive, or conservative - since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win, bidding your true value maximizes expected profit. With my value at $11, I should bid exactly $11 to ensure optimal outcomes: I win only when profitable (value exceeds the price I'd pay) and lose when it wouldn't be profitable.
